messages:
Maya: Heads-up — CI perf alert from the canary rollout for release/merge PR#3245. 99th latency jumped ~18% on the 8k seq tests. Noticed right after the kernel-selector change.
Sam: ugh. saw the alert too. which kernel change? the 'conv-opt' fallback in selector?
Maya: yeah, that one. config diff: we added a heuristic to prefer conv-opt for small batch sizes. on long sequences conv-opt seems to thrash KV cache.
Anita: any flamegraphs or perf profiles yet?
Maya: perf-bot uploaded a trace to the build: https://perf.internal/trace/2005004321 — root cause looks like increased L2 misses from kernel switching and extra cache flushes.
Sam: can you paste the top of the flame?
Maya: here's the snippet: ```
# top stacks
runtime::dispatch_kernel -> conv-opt::init -> kv_cache::spill -> memcpy
kv_cache::get -> conv-opt::prefetch -> stall_on_lock
```
Liam: conv-opt was meant to speed up short prompts by reducing compute ops. didn't expect KV churn on long prompts.
Anita: batch distribution on canary looks skewed — lots of single-request batches from the A/B traffic. the new heuristic bumps to conv-opt for those -> more kernel switches overall.
Maya: CI regression log: `canary-e2e-2005: p99 = 254ms (baseline 216ms)` — triggered the staged-rollout SLO gate, rollout paused automatically. deploy-bot: "staged rollout paused: perf SLO breach" :pause_button:.
deploy-bot: "Action: canary traffic sliced back to 5%; rollout paused at 40%"
Sam: ok first steps: replicate locally with synthetic that mimics long seq + single-item batches. Anita can you run `./scripts/run_local_profiler --seq 8192 --batch-dist single`?
Anita: running now, will attach trace.
Maya: I'd like a bisect on the kernel-selector commit range. suspect is commit 8f3d2 -> 8f3d9. if we confirm, we should revert selector tweak and re-run canary.
Liam: quick check: any quantization/compile flags changed in that release? compile flags stayed the same, just selector logic.
perf-bot: CI perf test failed threshold for test `long_sequence_slo` on builder-12. Diff: +18% p99. See CI build 2005004309.
Anita: profiling shows `kv_cache::lock` wait spikes aligned with kernel switches. snippet: ```
# psuedo
for req in batch:
  if selector.prefers(conv_opt):
    acquire(kv.lock)
    prefetch_kv(req)
    release(kv.lock)
```
we're grabbing the kv lock more often due to switch-induced prefetches.
Sam: two options: 1) add sticky-kernel policy to reduce fluctuations (prefer previous kernel unless strong signal) 2) revert selector heuristic and roll forward with a better gating test.
Maya: sticky-kernel sounds low-risk. could be a canary patch that reduces thrash. add a cooldown window (e.g., 250ms) so we don't flip per-request.
Liam: will that hurt short-batch latency improvements? possibly small regression for very short prompts but better overall SLOs.
Anita: I'm for sticky-kernel + adding a metric for kernel-switch-rate to the SLO dashboard. that would let the rollout guardrail catch this earlier.
Sam: agree. also add a synthetic CI test that injects single-item batch traffic with long sequences to catch this pattern.
Maya: action items: - Anita: run local repro and attach traces (ETA 20m) - Liam: prototype sticky-kernel flag + 250ms cooldown (ETA 2h) - Sam: bisect cluster to confirm culprit commit and stop-gap revert if needed (ETA 1h) - I'll notify product/onsite teams that canary is paused and we'll update status.
Anita: trace attached: https://perf.internal/attachments/2005004321/trace1 — kv lock wait went from median 0.6ms -> 4.2ms.
deploy-bot: "rollout status: paused, canary at 40% -> scaled down to 5% per SLO automation"
Sam: if Liam's sticky-kernel lands quickly we can try unpausing traffic to 20% and watch kernel-switch-rate + p99. would prefer that over full revert.
Maya: agreed. also add an alert on kernel-switch-rate > 0.05/s per instance for staged rollouts.
Liam: starting the PR now. will tag @Sam @Anita for review. keeping it small: flag + cooldown + unit tests.
Anita: reprod run finished — local p99 back to baseline with sticky-kernel sim. attaching results.
Maya: thanks. once PR is merged deploy-bot can trigger a canary resume. leave the staged rollout paused until we see 2 green canary cycles.
Sam: noted. I'll keep the bisect ready if perf worsens after sticky-kernel.
Maya: thanks everyone. keeping thread for updates. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
